title: Natural finite-coordinate stalk comparison for affine sheafification
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], x in an affine open U, A = Gamma(X,U), and R = O_{X,x} [def-pc-module-stalk-functor]. Let Phi = affinePerfectSheafification X U hU, the existing tilde/restriction/slice-equivalence functor [lem-pc-affine-perfect-module-model], and let T be ordinary open direct image followed by the ambient module stalk functor. Put E_B(n) = ULift(Fin(n) -> B). There are isomorphisms e_n : E_R(n) -> T(Phi(E_A(n))) for all n. For any A-linear f : E_A(n) -> E_A(m) and R-linear g : E_R(n) -> E_R(m), if every standard-basis coefficient of f has germ equal to the corresponding coefficient of g, then T(Phi(f)) e_n = e_m g. This compares individual free modules and their maps, with no complex, bounds, square-zero condition, or shrinking assertion.

proof.text: Use the existing affinePerfectSheafification functor, defined by tilde on Spec(A), restriction along the affine chart, and the inverse of overEquiv U. Its value on a coordinate module is the finite free sheaf on the standard basis.

The natural tilde stalk localization identifies a basis vector with its basis germ and localizes all its coefficients. Transport along the affine chart and the slice-site equivalence. In ordinary direct image, each neighbourhood V contained in U has the same sections as the local sheaf. These neighbourhoods are cofinal at x; taking their colimit therefore gives the ambient stalk with the identical scalar action. The finite basis germs give the isomorphisms e_n, including the empty basis.

Apply both sides of the proposed naturality equation to every standard basis vector. On the left the coordinates are the germs of f coefficients, by the natural associated-sheaf localization map. On the right they are the coefficients of g. The assumed coefficient equations make these equal. Equality on a finite basis proves the equality of R-linear maps.
